section.title: Introduction
section.para: The package opennlp.tools.noise detects possible optical character recognition (OCR) errors, repetitive text, and encoded binary data. Annotations on the opennlp:noise layer use these severities in increasing order: misspelled, damaged, gibberish, and binaryish. A score in (0, 1] indicates the strength of the evidence within that severity. It is not a probability. Scores from different severities are not comparable. Scoring does not change the text.

StructuralNoiseScorer uses rules and includes no model or dictionary. It examines whitespace-delimited tokens after trimming common ASCII punctuation. Cores shorter than 3 characters or containing non-ASCII characters are skipped. The rules count consonant runs, repeated characters, vowel proportions, and letter-digit transitions. Binary-content detection also checks length and case changes. A digit in a long identifier is insufficient for that category.

These heuristics can mark technical identifiers or unfamiliar words as noise and miss damaged text with ordinary letter patterns. An empty result is not a quality guarantee. The rules have no published accuracy benchmark.

section.title: Scoring text
section.para: Exclusions must fit within the text. Empty exclusions have no effect. A token that overlaps an exclusion is omitted, and results are not merged across excluded whitespace. Returned spans use UTF-16 offsets into the original text.
